candidate:
REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u3
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, white_key_made) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, grey_star_made) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, grey_star_on_right) -> u3
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, else) -> u3
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, white_key_made, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, grey_star_made, u2) -> 0.2
(u2, grey_star_on_right, u3) -> 1.0
feedback: Accepted. The RM is a faithful, minimal encoding of the task's three ordered stages: u0→u1 on white_key_made (rule 2 turns the purple ball into a white key), u1→u2 on grey_star_made (rule 1 turns the white key into a grey star), u2→u3 on grey_star_on_right (goal fires). (1) Ordered coverage / no skipping: the environment constraints (white keys only exist after rule 2 fires; grey stars only exist after rule 1 fires) guarantee white_key_made precedes grey_star_made precedes grey_star_on_right, and the per-state else self-loops make any out-of-order or irrelevant event inert, so neither stage can be shortcut. Since rule 1 runs before rule 2 in a step, white_key_made and grey_star_made cannot co-fire at u0, and the first grey_star_made cannot co-fire with grey_star_on_right (rule 1 places the star on the agent's left cell, not the right), so the one-specific-transition-per-state design is unambiguous. (2) Irrelevant events (grey_square_made, yellow_hex_made, green_key_made, green_ball_picked_up, white_pyramid_picked_up) are covered by else self-loops in every state, including the absorbing final state. (3) Event semantics: all supplied propositions are step events and the RM treats them strictly as one-step triggers with else-waiting; no persistent-state predicates are invented, and the transition/reward conditions use only events from the labeling API (products_made, goal_reached). (4) Reward safety: there is exactly one purple ball, hence at most one white_key_made, one white key hence at most one grey_star_made, and the episode ends on grey_star_on_right, so the positive progress rewards (0.1, 0.2) cannot be farmed by repeating; rewards are dense across the three stages, bounded, nonnegative, with the maximal reward 1.0 reserved for the goal entry, and unlisted transitions default to 0. (5) Regressions: none required — the task is a strictly increasing chain and each event is unique; the else self-loops already prevent wrong advancement. (6) Reachability: the reference trace (reset seed 1) realizes the exact chain in 65 steps, well under the 507 limit; u2→u3 is always completable because a blocked forward still counts for rules and the goal, and the agent can relocate the grey star if its grid-left neighbor is a wall. (7) Format: exact paper layout — REWARD_MACHINE header, declared STATES, INITIAL_STATE, nonempty FINAL_STATES whose sole member u3 is declared and accepting (entered only via the goal event, absorbing via its else self-loop with no reward), and a REWARD_FUNCTION whose triples all correspond to declared transitions. No defects found; review only, artifact stands as submitted.

feedback: All eight environment-declared propositions are defined exactly once, with no extra or missing functions, and each matches the documented truth condition from the code notes. The five 'made' events correctly read `"<tile>" in env.products_made`, the two pickup events read `env.picked_up == "<tile>"`, and the goal event reads `env.goal_reached`, consistent with every proposition being an event of the last step rather than a persistent grid state. All expressions return boolean values, use only the documented read-only API (`env.products_made`, `env.picked_up`, `env.goal_reached`), contain no imports, actions, side effects, or mutations of the environment or episode memory, and are syntactically valid Python. Unused-in-RM declared predicates (grey_square_made, yellow_hex_made, green_key_made, green_ball_picked_up, white_pyramid_picked_up) are correctly included since they are part of the declared proposition set.
